title: Schisandrin inhibits VSMCs proliferation and migration by arresting cell cycle and targeting JAK2 to regulating the JAK2/STAT3 pathway.
authors: Huang, Qiuxia; Liu, Xinyao; Yu, Jinjin; Liu, Yang; Song, Huixin; Zhang, Xinya; Zhou, Lili; Wang, Siqi; Niu, Xiaofeng; Li, Weifeng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究五味子素抑制血管平滑肌细胞增殖迁移的JAK2/STAT3通路机制，属细胞信号通路药理学研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模内容，与本课题无关。
abstract: Abnormal proliferation, migration, and foam cell formation of Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) each play a role in the development of atherosclerosis (AS). Schisandrin (Sch) is the active lignan ingredient with broad-spectrum pharmacological effects. However, the role of Sch in the AS process is not clear. Therefore, this study was proposed to explore the therapeutic effect and potential mechanism of Sch on VSMCs. Ox-LDL was selected to create an atherosclerosis injury environment for VSMCs and macrophages. The MTT assay, Oil red O staining, wound healing, transwell experiments and ELISA were used to investigate the phenotype effects of Sch. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, flow cytometry, and western blot were used to investigate the underlying mechanisms of Sch on AS progression. Our findings implied that Sch treatment inhibited the proliferation and migration of VSMCs, and suppressed the ROS production and inflammatory cytokines up-regulation of VSMCs and macrophages. Moreover, Sch reduced lipid uptake and foam cell formation through downregulating LOX-1. Mechanistically, we found that Sch can inhibit the activation of JAK2/STAT3 signaling by targeting JAK2, and arrest cell cycle in GO/G1 phase. In summary, Sch can inhibit VSMCs proliferation and migration by arresting cell cycle and targeting JAK2 to regulating the JAK2/STAT3 pathway. Sch may serve as a potential drug for patients with AS.
abstract_zh: 血管平滑肌细胞（VSMCs）的异常增殖、迁移及泡沫细胞形成均在动脉粥样硬化（AS）的发展中发挥作用。五味子素（Sch）是具有广谱药理作用的活性木脂素成分。然而，Sch在AS过程中的作用尚不明确。因此，本研究旨在探讨Sch对VSMCs的治疗效果及其潜在机制。选用氧化低密度脂蛋白（Ox-LDL）构建VSMCs和巨噬细胞的动脉粥样硬化损伤环境。采用MTT实验、油红O染色、伤口愈合实验、Transwell实验和ELISA法研究Sch的表型效应。通过网络药理学、分子对接、流式细胞术和蛋白质印迹法探讨Sch对AS进展的潜在机制。研究结果表明，Sch处理抑制了VSMCs的增殖和迁移，并抑制了VSMCs和巨噬细胞中ROS的产生及炎症细胞因子的上调。此外，Sch通过下调LOX-1减少了脂质摄取和泡沫细胞形成。机制上，我们发现Sch可通过靶向JAK2抑制JAK2/STAT3信号通路的激活，并将细胞周期阻滞在G0/G1期。总之，Sch可通过阻滞细胞周期并靶向JAK2调控JAK2/STAT3通路，从而抑制VSMCs的增殖和迁移。Sch可能成为AS患者的潜在治疗药物。
